title: Prehistoric India: The Stone Age Foundations

questions.question: 'Prehistory' refers to the period:
options: Before written records, known only through material remains
questions.rationale: Prehistory covers the human past lacking written documents; scholars reconstruct it from stone tools, pottery, bones, ash, and rock art.

questions.question: The correct cultural sequence of Indian prehistory is:
questions.rationale: Old Stone Age (knapped tools) → Middle (microliths) → New (farming, polished tools, pottery) → Copper-Stone villages.

questions.question: The rock shelters of Bhimbetka, famous for prehistoric paintings, are located in:
questions.rationale: Bhimbetka (Raisen district, MP) — a UNESCO site discovered for science by V. S. Wakankar — holds paintings from Mesolithic times onward in red and white ochre.

questions.question: Microliths, tiny stone blades set into wood or bone with resin, characterise which age?
questions.rationale: Mesolithic hunters targeted small game and fish using these composite tools — light, versatile tips for arrows and spears.

questions.question: Mehrgarh, the earliest Neolithic farming village of the subcontinent (c. 7000 BCE), lies in:
questions.rationale: Mehrgarh in Balochistan grew wheat and barley and cultivated cotton — the ancestor settlement of the later Harappan tradition.

questions.question: Pit-dwellings — circular pits dug into the ground as house foundations — characterise which Neolithic site?
questions.rationale: Burzahom's people lived in pits (warm in winter, cool in summer) with mud-plastered sides and thatched roofs, alongside polished stone and bone tools.

questions.question: Which is a Chalcolithic culture of Maharashtra known from Inamgaon and Daimabad?
questions.rationale: The Jorwe culture (c. 1400–700 BCE) built planned farming villages in the northern Deccan; Ahar–Banas, Kayatha, and Malwa are its western-central contemporaries.

questions.question: In Chalcolithic Jorwe villages, children were often buried:
options: In separate cemeteries outside the village
Under house floors in pairs of urns joined mouth-to-mouth
questions.rationale: Two urns placed mouth-to-mouth under the house floor held the child's remains — a domestic ritual echoed at Inamgaon and Nevasa.

questions.question: Ash-mound Neolithic sites associated with cattle herding, like Piklihal and Utnur, are found in:
questions.rationale: Southern Neolithic herders penning cattle built up mounds of burnt dung and ash — Piklihal, Utnur, Maski, Brahmagiri — while growing ragi and horsegram.

questions.question: The large-scale clearing of Gangetic forests became possible only with the arrival of:
questions.rationale: Soft copper could not fell dense monsoon forest; iron axes of the Painted Grey Ware era cleared land for settled agriculture, enabling the Mahajanapadas.
